## Left open by the earlier read (RD-123)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B01 (Blocker). Problem: This makes payment a universal starting condition. The processing-time rule requires payment only when a fee applies. A complete fee-free request does not need a payment before its processing clock can start.
   > Processing starts with complete requirements and payment.
2. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The processing-start condition omits that payment applies only when applicable. Students need that limit to avoid treating fee-free requests as outside the stated processing deadlines.
   > Processing starts with complete requirements and payment.

### Accuracy concerns

1. Payment is stated without the applicable-fee condition. Fee-free transactions also have processing deadlines once their requirements are complete.
   > Processing starts with complete requirements and payment.
